format: Pokemon Champions VGC 2026 Regulation M-B / doubles BO3 / ranked-ladder-style high ladder

Season M-5 starts August 5 2026 and ends September 9 2026.
Newly usable Pokemon include Mega Staraptor, Mega Tyranitar-related ecosystem pieces, Gholdengo, Grimmsnarl, Mega Swampert, Mega Metagross, Mega Blaziken, Mega Sceptile, Mega Mawile, etc.

observations: Completed tournament list around Aug 8-10 included many Champions/Reg M-B events: Sketch Academy, VGC Reg M-B Ingame Tour, The Drywalls Series, Intimidators Champions Challenge, Pokepal Smackdown, etc.

labmaus_top_six_compositions_by_score.archetype: Tailwind/Floette balance with priority and Intimidate-resistant pressure

primary_archetypes_and_plans.plan: Deny free Intimidate value with Competitive; use Tailwind/Icy Wind to avoid pure sand-speed ties; preserve Tyranitar until Excadrill can clean.

Lead weather/speed control immediately: Mega Tyranitar flips sun to sand and enables Sand Rush. Rock Slide pressure threatens Charizard/Whimsicott; Milotic handles Garchomp with Icy Wind/Ice Beam and discourages Incineroar pivots. Keep Gholdengo benched unless they lack Garchomp/Kingambit pressure.

Contest rain at lead. Excadrill threatens Archaludon and Grimmsnarl; Tyranitar removes rain and pressures Pelipper. Sinistcha gives Rage Powder/Hospitality into Basculegion/Archaludon turns. Gholdengo exploits passive screens turns with Nasty Plot and blocks status/control.

Milotic punishes Incineroar and keeps speed control with Icy Wind. Staraptor threatens Sneasler/Kingambit with Brave Bird/Close Combat and Tailwind. Gholdengo is strong into Sinistcha and ignores many status/control lines; Sinistcha protects it from single-target pressure.

threats: Farigiraf blocking priority and setting Trick Room
primary_archetypes_and_plans.plan: Use sand to reverse speed. Excadrill Iron Head/Rock Slide pressures Aerodactyl/Sylveon/Charizard; Tyranitar checks Charizard and removes items. Milotic covers Garchomp. Gholdengo gives a non-physical route if Intimidate/Farigiraf slows physical endgame.

Do not give them free tempo. Rock Slide/Iron Head chip breaks sashes; sand chip matters. Staraptor handles Sneasler/Kingambit if positioned safely; Milotic stabilizes with Icy Wind/Scald and discourages Intimidate users if present.

general_decision_rules: Default bring is often Tyranitar-Mega + Excadrill + Staraptor-Mega + Milotic when the opponent is fast, Charizard/Garchomp-heavy, or weather-dependent.
Bring Gholdengo + Sinistcha together when the opponent relies on status, redirection wars, passive screens turns, or lacks immediate Ground/Dark pressure.
Milotic is the anti-Incineroar and anti-Garchomp stabilizer; avoid leaving it home into Incineroar/Garchomp unless rain pressure forces Gholdengo/Sinistcha.
Staraptor is both Tailwind and immediate Fighting/Flying pressure; it is especially important into Kingambit/Sneasler/Venusaur but must respect Rock Slide and Sash trades.
Tyranitar should be preserved for weather re-entry against Charizard/Pelipper; do not spend it early if losing sand lets Basculegion/Charizard sweep.
Excadrill is the clearest closer under sand; protect its Focus Sash from chip/status where possible and use Sinistcha redirection when expecting single-target Fighting/Ground moves.
